data.task: Compare Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.8 Flash (High thinking), and Gemini 3.1 Pro for editing an existing production React drill page, including Tailwind spacing, UI hierarchy, and preserving component state.

recommendation.why: This is a surgical maintenance task rather than greenfield UI generation. Opus 4.6 has the strongest directly relevant evidence for navigating large codebases, identifying the right changes, code review/debugging, long-running work, and retaining details in large context. Those traits best map to making a minimal Tailwind/UI change without accidentally rewriting stateful React logic.
recommendation.caveat: No source found in this run reports a controlled head-to-head test specifically on Tailwind spacing edits or React component-state preservation. The ranking is therefore an evidence-based fit judgment, not a direct task benchmark.
recommendation.recommended_workflow: Ask the model to inspect the existing component and its state/handlers first; constrain the patch to layout/class changes; require a diff; explicitly prohibit changing keys, state initialization, event handlers, data flow, or component boundaries; then run the page and regression checks.

ranking.fit: Best overall for a production React drill-page spacing adjustment where preserving behavior is more important than generating a novel visual design.
evidence: Anthropic says Opus 4.6 plans more carefully, operates more reliably in larger codebases, and improves code review and debugging.
Anthropic describes its ability to navigate a large codebase and identify the right changes as state of the art, and reports improved design-system work.
The model has a 1M-token context window in beta, context compaction, adaptive thinking, and configurable effort; Anthropic reports 76% on the 8-needle 1M MRCR v2 variant, versus 18.5% for Sonnet 4.5.
Its published SWE-bench Verified score is 80.8%, narrowly above Gemini 3.1 Pro's 80.6% in the independent comparison source.
risks_or_tradeoffs: higher cost and potentially higher latency than Flash
may overthink a simple spacing-only change; Anthropic recommends lowering effort from high to medium when appropriate

ranking.fit: Strong alternative, and potentially the best of the three for visual hierarchy/front-end ideation; second for this production-maintenance task because the priority is a safe localized edit with state preserved.
evidence: Google positions 3.1 Pro for complex tasks and shows it generating website-ready animated SVGs, translating APIs into user-friendly dashboards, and producing interactive/creative web designs.
A frontend-focused code-review source reports 1,487 Elo on WebDev Arena, described as the top tested score for frontend, and specifically calls out React/Vue/frontend frameworks.
The same source reports 80.6% SWE-bench Verified, only 0.2 points below Opus 4.6, but also says it is weaker on long multi-step reasoning and complex PRs than Claude.
The comparison source reports Gemini leading some broad/competitive coding and tool-coordination measures, including LiveCodeBench Pro and MCP Atlas, at much lower listed token prices than Opus.
strengths_for_this_task: good alternative when the prompt includes screenshots or design intent
risks_or_tradeoffs: less compelling than Opus for conservative multi-step production changes
frontend Arena and code-review results are not the same as a controlled Tailwind/state-preservation test
source claims about a 2M context window conflict with Google's announcement page, which does not state that number; do not rely on it without verifying the serving endpoint

ranking.fit: Best value/throughput option and plausible choice for a simple, well-scoped spacing pass, but third when an existing production page must retain component state and avoid collateral changes.
evidence: Google calls 3.8 Flash its best reasoning and coding model at the speed and low cost of 3.7 Flash, with improvements across software engineering and agentic tasks.

Google says the model works harder at higher effort levels, taking extra reasoning steps and making iterative tool calls; this supports using High for a more careful pass but may increase token use and latency.
Google reports 3.8 Flash at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through December 31, 2026, with higher introductory pricing afterward.

The independent Vellum analysis reports strong shaped coding results (73.7% DeepSWE v1.1 and 89.4% Terminal-Bench 2.1), but a large gap on general-agent Terminal-Bench 4.0 (19.1% versus Opus 5's 51.8%). This suggests strong execution/value, but less confidence for broad production context management.
strengths_for_this_task: High effort can spend more reasoning on a constrained patch
risks_or_tradeoffs: less evidence for conservative React maintenance and state preservation than Opus
higher thinking effort can consume more tokens
general-agent results in the available analysis show a substantial ceiling gap, and there is no direct Tailwind/React-state evaluation

editing_existing_react_components.reason: The task favors codebase navigation, targeted diffs, debugging, and long-context consistency over greenfield generation.

tailwind_css_spacing_adjustments.reason: 3.1 Pro has the strongest frontend/UI-specific evidence; Opus is the safer production-editing choice. This is a judgment, not a direct Tailwind benchmark.

ui_hierarchy.reason: Google's examples emphasize design intent, interactive design, dashboards, and website-ready code; Opus has supporting evidence for design-system quality.

preserving_component_state.reason: Preservation is primarily a repository-context, restraint, and regression-risk problem. Opus has the clearest published evidence for large-codebase navigation, code review/debugging, long context, and identifying the right changes.

data.bottom_line: Choose Claude Opus 4.6 for the actual production drill-page patch. Choose Gemini 3.1 Pro if visual hierarchy/design quality is the dominant concern or if cost matters substantially. Choose Gemini 3.8 Flash in High mode for inexpensive, repeatable, tightly constrained iterations after the required files and invariants are explicitly specified.

message: Compared the three models using official vendor pages plus frontend/coding benchmark analyses. Recommendation: Claude Opus 4.6 for the production React spacing patch; Gemini 3.1 Pro is the strongest UI/frontend alternative; Gemini 3.8 Flash High is the value/throughput option. The sources do not provide a controlled benchmark specifically for Tailwind spacing or React state preservation, so that part is an evidence-based fit judgment.
